citations.text: Efklides, A., & Schwartz, B. L. (2024). Revisiting the Metacognitive and Affective Model of Self-Regulated Learning: Origins, Development, and Future Directions. Educational Psychology Review, 36, 61.

en.general: Deliberate, domain-free ways of controlling the course of one's work and checking it: orienting to the task, planning, monitoring how the plan is carried out and evaluating the result. The article calls them typical of top-down regulation and separates them from strategies that work only within one subject.

examples: A student plans her study hours before an exam.
A student checks halfway through whether the plan is working.
nonExamples: A rule for simplifying equations, which applies only in mathematics.
